_what_this_is: Records the version of each upstream dependency that a human has actually REVIEWED. A test asserts each of these equals the version the build RESOLVED. Every dependency floats to latest at build time, so when upstream publishes, that test goes red and the release gate cannot pass until this file is updated.
_stop_before_you_edit_this_file: Read UPSTREAM-REVIEW.md and follow it. Bumping a version here without doing the review defeats the only mechanism that catches upstream behaviour changes, renamed config keys and changed defaults. None of those are visible to the golden tools/list snapshot, and loadConfig is a bare JSON.parse with no schema validation, so a renamed key is discarded in silence.
_notes_are_not_optional: Every bump records what changed, what was adopted, and what was explicitly declined and why. A decline with a reason is worth as much as an adoption: it stops the same question being re-litigated at the next bump. An empty note is a review that did not happen.
_this_file_is_gated: Not by a prompt. Editing this file is unrestricted; what is gated is the RELEASE. The build regenerates four snapshots from the resolved payload -- tools/list, --help, config.d.ts, browsers.json -- and diffs them, runs the full suite, and asserts that this file adjudicates whatever actually moved and answers every manual re-verification row by name. An entry that ignores what the build observed fails the build. See TESTING.md, 'The upstream-review gate'.
_correction_2026_08_15: An earlier version of the note above said a PreToolUse hook asks a human to approve every edit, and that a sub-agent attempting one is killed silently. Both halves were wrong, and measurement disproved them: under permission_mode 'bypassPermissions' a hook's 'ask' returned to a sub-agent is silently downgraded to ALLOW -- the edit lands unprompted, and the gate was inert against exactly the caller most likely to need it. A sub-agent did die during that work, but not from the hook; the cause is unknown and its transcript was zero bytes. Recorded because a confident wrong explanation is worse than an admitted gap, which is the same rule this file applies to versions.

@playwright/mcp.why_it_matters: Ships in the payload. Its CLI surface and config schema are what BrowserAI generates against, and both change without notice.
@playwright/mcp.notes: Reviewed 0.0.79 -> 0.0.80 on 2026-09-14. Published 2026-09-01 on dist-tag latest; 7 commits between the tags. WHAT UPSTREAM CHANGED IN ITS OWN TREE: NOTHING UNDER src/. The diff v0.0.79..v0.0.80 touches 8 files and not one is product source -- .azure-pipelines/publish.yml, .github/dependabot.yml, .github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/workflows/publish.yml, README.md, package-lock.json, package.json, server.json. THE TWO DIFFS UPSTREAM-REVIEW.md CALLS THE HIGHEST-VALUE READS BOTH CAME BACK EMPTY: tests/ is byte-identical and config.d.ts is byte-identical across the bump. So the ENTIRE product-facing change of this version is the playwright-core roll (commit 105c7b9, 'chore: roll Playwright to 1.63.0-alpha-2026-08-31'), and it is adjudicated in the playwright-core entry. The two new tool names reach upstream's README only because that file is generated by running the server, which is why they appear in a diff that touches no source. SNAPSHOTS, all four regenerated from the rebuilt payload and diffed: cli-help.txt UNCHANGED (byte-identical -- the --output-mode class is clear), config-schema.d.ts UNCHANGED (byte-identical -- the SILENT class is clear, no config key renamed, removed or added), tools-list.json CHANGED, browsers.json CHANGED. tools-list.json ADJUDICATED: the three resolvedFrom stamps and serverInfo.version moved with the versions; counts internalRegistry 78 -> 80 and exposedMaximum 69 -> 71, while defaultSurface (24) and skillOnly (9, the same nine names) did not move; TWO TOOLS ADDED -- browser_start_recording and browser_stop_recording, both capability devtools (11 -> 13), both with an empty inputSchema and readOnlyHint true. ZERO removed, ZERO renamed, and NOT ONE SURVIVING TOOL'S DEFINITION CHANGED AT ALL -- asserted by diffing the two accepted snapshots entry by entry, schema included, rather than by reading a changelog; the order of the surviving tools is preserved, which is what lossless passthrough rests on, and the protocol ceiling is still 2025-11-25. browsers.json ADJUDICATED: chromium 1237 -> 1243 (152.0.7977.8 -> 153.0.8010.12), chromium-headless-shell the same pair, firefox 1539 -> 1542 (153.0 -> 155.0), webkit 2342 -> 2358 with browserVersion 26.5 and the two mac revisionOverrides unchanged; ffmpeg 1011, winldd 1007 and android 1001 unmoved. CONSEQUENCE, AND A RELEASE-NOTES LINE IS OWED: every machine re-provisions. The suite measured it rather than predicting it -- the first-run arm pulled 203.8 MB from the CDN in 23.6 s because every cached tree was refused, the cache holding chromium-1237 while this build wants chromium-1243. A ROLLBACK RE-DOWNLOADS TOO, which is the half the release notes have to say. The test rig was re-provisioned as part of this batch, and upstream's own installer PRUNED firefox-1539 while installing chromium-1243, so Firefox had to be reinstalled at 1542 or the Firefox arms would have skipped and the gate would have reported reduced coverage as a clean run. PAYLOAD: the mcp tree went 18,997,245 -> 18,623,990 b (-373,255), and fsevents left the resolved lock entirely -- it was an optional macOS-only transitive of playwright -- so the tree is now three packages rather than four. No package in it declares an install script, which the payload build asserts rather than assumes. DECLINED, with reasons: (1) the whole devops half -- the new ESRP publishing pipeline, dropping scheduled @next publishing, pinning GitHub Actions to full-length SHAs, adding dependabot -- none of it is consumed here, because the payload build resolves from the npm registry by dist-tag and never touches upstream's CI; (2) the next dist-tag, which read 0.0.79-alpha-1787869812000 on this date and is deliberately not tracked; (3) server.json's version bump, which is the MCP registry's metadata and not something this product reads. *** NOT ADOPTED, AND NOT ADOPTABLE BY THIS BATCH: THE TWO NEW TOOLS HAVE NO VERDICT. *** BrowserAI denies by default, so a call naming either is already refused at the door -- but an ABSENT row is a gap rather than a decision, so both are still advertised in tools/list, which is ToolVerdicts' deliberate design. tool-verdicts.json was LEFT UNTOUCHED, judgedAgainst included: moving that stamp to 0.0.80 / 1.63.0-alpha-2026-08-31 would assert that the file HAS been re-judged against this tool set, and it has not. The last complete judgement really was against 0.0.79, and the stamp says so. Seven suite arms are red on that one pending decision and no others: ToolVerdictTests.EveryToolInTheSnapshotHasAVerdictAndEveryVerdictNamesAToolInTheSnapshot (names both tools), ToolVerdictTests.TheJudgementsNameTheUpstreamThisBuildResolved (the stamp), ToolVerdictTests.TheCoverageComparisonFailsInBothDirectionsAgainstADoctoredFile (its planted control expects exactly one disagreement and finds three), RecordedCountTests.TheToolSurfaceNumbersInDecisionsAreWhatTheSnapshotHolds, ModelSurfaceTests.EverySessionGetsEveryCapabilityAndTheNewlyGrantedTenAreInTheSurface, SessionPolicyTests.ASessionPermitsEveryToolItAdvertisesAndTheOneThatWouldHangIsNotAdvertised and VerticalSliceTests.ToolsListReturnsTheChildsToolsWithUpstreamsOwnNames. The numbers those last four hold are NOT written here, deliberately: each depends on whether the two tools are allowed or denied, and writing the allow-both figure would record an adoption nobody made. WHAT WAS UPDATED BECAUSE IT DOES NOT DEPEND ON THE VERDICT: UpstreamSnapshotTests.TheCapabilityFilterReproducesTheRecordedSurfaces 42 -> 44 and 69 -> 71, kb/playwright/tools-and-artifacts.md's per-capability table, re-verification row 11, and README's 78/69 sentence. Those are properties of upstream's surface before this product withholds anything, so they do not move again when the verdict lands. *** ADJUDICATED 2026-09-15, AND THE GAP IS CLOSED. *** The maintainer judged both new tools `allow` (Q163 = a), on a measurement taken before the judgement rather than on the shape of their names: browser_start_recording returns in 40-46 ms and ARMS a recorder rather than waiting for a human, every other tool answers normally while a recording is live, and browser_stop_recording returns Playwright code -- so the liveness shape that withholds browser_annotate does not reach them. Both rows were added to tool-verdicts.json in upstream's own order, judgedAgainst was moved to 0.0.80 / 1.63.0-alpha-2026-08-31, and browser_annotate is still the only denial. The counts that moved with it were RE-MEASURED rather than incremented: DECISIONS.md 69 -> 71 carried and 68 -> 70 advertised, SessionPolicyTests.Advertises 68 -> 70, VerticalSliceTests Names.Count + 68 -> + 70, ModelSurfaceTests 58 + ten -> 60 + ten, the kb's session-permits row 68 of 69 -> 70 of 71, and re-verification rows 12 and 69. The denied count is unchanged at 1 and the withheld count is unchanged at 1. The eight red arms this review left behind went to zero on the adoption batch's own gate.

playwright-core.why_it_matters: Carries the actual tool implementations and the browsers.json that pins the Chromium revision. Arrives as @playwright/mcp's own exact dependency, not as a choice we make.
playwright-core.notes: Reviewed 1.63.0-alpha-2026-08-05 -> 1.63.0-alpha-2026-08-31 on 2026-09-14. 26 days of daily alphas, adopted in one step because it arrives as @playwright/mcp 0.0.80's own EXACT dependency and there is no intermediate version this build could resolve. npm latest for playwright-core read 1.63.0 on this date -- a STABLE release, NEWER by SemVer than the alpha that ships -- so the wrong answer would have looked like the right one. It was not taken. HOW IT WAS READ: the two PUBLISHED TARBALLS were downloaded and diffed, not the git repository, because the bundle is what runs. coreBundle.js 3,449,273 -> 3,469,825 b (+20,552), 843 hunks. FOUND, each adjudicated: (1) TWO TOOLS ADDED -- browser_start_recording and browser_stop_recording. They are upstream's, they arrive here, and they have NO VERDICT; see the @playwright/mcp entry, which owns that stop. (2) THE chromiumSandbox CONFIG KEY IS NOW HONOURED. microsoft/playwright#42288 has arrived. The single line 'options.sandbox = options.sandbox === true ? void 0 : false;' is the only removal inside decorateMCPCommand's action, and everything downstream of it -- configFromCLIOptions, validateBrowserConfig's non-Linux branch, and the launcher's push of --no-sandbox when chromiumSandbox is not true -- is byte-identical. THE OUTCOME WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN DEDUCED FROM THAT, because the commander semantics in between are exactly what nobody should reason about: with chromiumSandbox true in a hand-written config and NO flag, 0 of the live browser's processes carried --no-sandbox, against 6 on the previous pin. THIS REPOSITORY PREDICTED IT AND THE PREDICTION HELD IN BOTH HALVES -- kb/playwright/configuration.md has carried the PR, its mechanism and its consequence since 2026-08-17, and said BrowserAI would be sandboxed on both sides because it passes --sandbox on the command line. It is. ADOPTED AS A FACT, NOT AS A CHANGE: SandboxFlagTests' second arm was inverted and renamed (and gained a non-vacuousness guard it did not need while it asserted a positive, because asserting zero is satisfied for free by a browser that never started), and the kb entry, ChildLaunch's doc comment and re-verification rows 3 and 102 were corrected. DECLINED, with the reason: dropping --sandbox from the command line now that upstream's default agrees with it. That would make this product's security posture rest on a default which has just been measured to move. The flag stays; it is belt and braces rather than the only thing that works. (3) scaleImageToFitMessage HAS BEEN DELETED, and this is the finding with a decision behind it. The function is GONE from the bundle (0 occurrences, and the constant 1568 with it), and the new screenshot backend no longer imports imageUtils or webp at all: the image content block is pushed straight from the capture. MEASURED end to end against the resolved payload, node v24.21.0 and chromium-1243: the inline block is now BYTE-IDENTICAL to the file on disk -- 22,186 b, 1920x1080, identical bytes true -- where before it was scaled down to at most 1568 px on a side and RE-ENCODED (recorded 2026-08-26 at the same viewport: 9,379 b on disk against 379,731 b inline). So an inline image is now larger in PIXELS and very much smaller in BYTES, and token cost follows pixels. NOT ADOPTED AND NOT PAPERED OVER: VerticalSliceTests.AScreenshotComesBackInlineAsWellAsAsAFileWithALegibleName is red on its 1568 bound and was deliberately LEFT red, because the sentence in the server instructions -- that fullPage costs the per-image token maximum because it leaves at full document height and is downscaled to that ceiling -- is now FALSE, there being no ceiling and no downscaling, and that string is model-facing. What to do about it is a product decision and is reported rather than taken. (4) PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_CODEGEN ADDED, inside the config env mapping. Row 17 RE-MEASURED rather than incremented, with the old bundle as the positive control: the same predicate returned 40 in the mapping + 2 outside = 42 against the old pin, which is exactly the recorded figure, and 41 + 2 = 43 against the new. No product change: the child environment is an ALLOWLIST, so a variable nobody named is absent by construction. It was deliberately NOT added to ChildEnvironment.Refused, which names variables that redirect a decision the config generator already took. (5) --codegen's default string became interpolated where it was the literal typescript. cli-help.txt is byte-identical across the bump, which is what says it still evaluates to typescript -- reading the template would have said nothing. (6) browserInfo on the ATTACHED path now carries browserName. BrowserAI never attaches to a running browser, so it is unreachable from here. CHECKED AND UNCHANGED, each read against BOTH bundles rather than assumed: the install-browser remediation template is BYTE-IDENTICAL -- throwIfExecutableMissing still builds the same sentence with 'npx @playwright/mcp install-browser <target>' inside backticks, so ProvisioningRemediation's anchored regex and its install-browser marker still match, and the real-child canary arm confirmed it live; winldd's chrome-win against Chromium's chrome-win64 is still the permanent no-op (row 10), so no new per-cold-start validation cost arrived; outputMaxSize still has no default (row 8); setupExitWatchdog and gracefullyCloseAll are unchanged (row 36); the cdn.playwright.dev mirror list and the /dbazure/download/playwright prefix are unchanged (row 72); redactSecrets is still a substring replaceAll over the whole serialised response (row 113); the dashboard's headedness is still gated on PWTEST_DASHBOARD_APP_BIND_TITLE, so browser_annotate's refusal is still earned (row 94); the chromiumSandbox resolution chain and the launcher's --no-sandbox push are byte-identical. Rows 13, 14, 20, 22, 67 and 106 are unchanged by inspection of the same anchors. Row 34 (Firefox cost ratios) and row 38 (resume cost) are OWED and were not re-run: both browser revisions moved and re-running them is a measurement session rather than a gate. browsers.json is adjudicated in the @playwright/mcp entry, which is where the snapshot lives.

ModelContextProtocol.why_it_matters: The protocol implementation on both sides of the proxy. Its typed layer drops unknown properties and throws on unknown content types, which is correct for a client and lossy for a proxy.
ModelContextProtocol.notes: Baseline. Tier 1 SDK under the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation; day-to-day engineering by the Microsoft .NET team. Declares IsAotCompatible=true on every non-netstandard2.0 target -- the author's claim about their code, not a proof for our usage. Full 2026-07-28 protocol support. Note 2.x drops MTP v1 in the 4.0.0 line of xUnit only; unrelated to this package.

Velopack.why_it_matters: Owns the update path, which is the most hazard-dense section of the charter. Five of its nine documented landmines were hit in production by a shipped product examined for this project rather than avoided.
Velopack.notes: Baseline. That product runs 0.0.1298 (pre-1.0), so nothing learned there transfers without re-verification against 1.2.0.

node.why_it_matters: Bundled in the payload as a single node.exe. A major bump changes size and can change process/stdio behaviour.
node.notes: Reviewed v24.20.0 -> v24.21.0 on 2026-09-14. Same Krypton LTS line. nodejs.org/dist/index.json -- which is what the payload build reads -- gives the release date as 2026-09-07, and the changelog's own header says September 8; the one-day difference is upstream's and changes nothing here. npm 11.19.0 and V8 13.6.233.17 are UNCHANGED; openssl 3.5.7 -> 3.5.8 is the only component that moved; security:false. WHAT WAS ADOPTED: the whole patch. The payload was rebuilt so the build's own resolver took it. node.exe grew 93,381,448 -> 93,580,104 b (+198,656); archive node-v24.21.0-win-x64.zip, sha256 158f7685b44de51f6c0df1d153526cbcd3e1bc739a8dfc607721cef75de9e541; LICENSE still at node-v24.21.0-win-x64/LICENSE and still 160,555 b. HOW IT WAS READ: this product uses node.exe for exactly two things -- running @playwright/mcp's cli.js over stdio pipes, and running cli.js install-browser -- so the release was read against those rather than as a whole. CLEARED BY MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN BY READING: 'crypto: update root certificates to NSS 3.126' and 'deps: update OpenSSL to 3.5.8' are the two items with a live failure mode, because provisioning downloads from Playwright's CDN over TLS. Both were EXERCISED in this batch rather than reasoned about -- install-browser firefox under this exact node.exe fetched firefox-win64.zip from cdn.playwright.dev and completed, and the suite's first-run arm then pulled 203.8 MB from the CDN in 23.6 s. WATCHED: 'child_process: keep SIGWINCH from killing on Win' (#64510) is the one Windows item touching the shape this product runs -- node as a parent of the browser processes -- and it is covered by the containment tiers rather than read: JobContainmentTests, JobObjectTests, BrowserContainmentTests and VerticalSliceTests.KillingThePublishedBinaryLeavesNoNodeAndNoBrowser are all green under v24.21.0. 'fs: fix realpath of namespaced drive paths' (#65378), 'fs: add windowsHandle option to file streams' (#63851) and 'src: expose Windows-only fs open flags' (#64775) are the other Windows-adjacent items; none changed a path taken here, and the whole-slice arms exercise the ones that could. DECLINED, each with its reason: (1) the two task-runner commits (#65217 escaping Windows environment variables, #64907 matching cmd.exe case-insensitively) -- that is node --run, which nothing here invokes; (2) the 16 stream commits -- overwhelmingly web streams and their hot paths, which playwright-core does not use for a piped child, and the classic-stream items are covered by the real-child and smoke tiers rather than by reading them; (3) every SEMVER-MINOR in the release -- crypto STORE-loader private keys, the histogram rework, net.BlockList performance, perf_hooks hypothesis testing, util.MIMEType.parse -- none is on a path BrowserAI takes, and NODE_OPTIONS and NODE_PATH are refused at ChildEnvironment.Refused so no new flag can arrive through the environment; (4) 'deps: update Undici to 7.29.1' -- playwright-core brings its own HTTP for the CDN, and nothing here calls fetch from node; (5) 'tty: add raw-vt and io raw modes' -- the child's stdio are pipes and every launch in this tree sets CreateNoWindow, so there is no tty to put in a raw mode; (6) npm is unchanged in any case, and the payload extracts only node.exe and LICENSE from the archive, so the bundled npm ships nowhere and resolves nothing. RE-VERIFICATION (kb/re-verification.md), every row a Node move puts in play, answered by name: rows 2 and 2b (job containment end to end, and from the published NativeAOT binary) -- ANSWERED GREEN by the gate under v24.21.0, ILCompiler 10.0.12 and SDK 10.0.401; row 21 (payload sizes) -- the two PAYLOAD rows were re-measured by this build and both figures are updated in place, and the FOUR BROWSER figures are OWED AND NOT RUN because both browser revisions moved, which the row now says in place rather than carrying the old numbers forward as if they still held; row 26 (payload licensing as shipped) -- re-read, Node's LICENSE is still the single aggregated file at the same size and the payload's licensing composition is unchanged; row 46 (Node's LICENSE is not published beside node.exe, and the extraction is keyed on the archive path) -- ANSWERED by the build, which found and extracted node-v24.21.0-win-x64/LICENSE and would have thrown had the archive been restructured; row 49 (npm lock keying, and npm ci not rewriting the lock) -- ANSWERED, the rebuild parsed the lock with -AsHashtable and npm ci left it byte-identical, which the build asserts rather than observes; row 50 (PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD gates only the postinstall paths) -- ANSWERED, and for the first time on a build that actually installed: the variable was set throughout and the explicit install-browser chromium still provisioned, which is the behaviour the payload build's comment predicts and the reason it fails loudly on the chrome.exe assertion if upstream ever extends the gate; row 85 (the update lane's own numbers) -- OWED AND STILL NOT RUN, and the kb entry says so in place, dated, now naming a THREE-sided gap rather than one: node.exe +198,656 on the day and +754,688 since the figures were taken, the payload mcp tree DOWN 373,255, and the published BrowserAI.exe at 19,186,688 against the recorded 17,853,952. NOT ONE FIGURE WAS ADJUSTED, and the two payload halves moved in opposite directions, so there is not even a single delta a reader could be tempted to add. Rows 16 and 16a are NOT in play: their trigger is an SDK change to the discover probe, not a Node move. Row 102 IS in play but on the @playwright/mcp axis rather than this one, and it is answered in the playwright-core entry -- it ARRIVED. v26 is Current rather than LTS and is deliberately not tracked; it read v26.8.2 on this date.

_chromium_is_derived: Chromium, ffmpeg and winldd revisions are NOT listed here. They follow from the resolved playwright-core's browsers.json and are recorded in the release's resolved-set manifest instead. Reviewing playwright-core covers them.
